summary: 高欢第九子，孝昭崩后即位，改元太宁、河清，颁律令；然荒淫委任佞幸，河清四年禅位太子纬，自称太上皇，天统五年崩。
summary_en: Ninth son of Gao Huan, he took the throne after Xiaozhao's death, changing the eras to Taining and Heqing and issuing the statutes; but he gave himself to debauchery and trusted flatterers, and in the 4th year of Heqing abdicated to his heir Wei, styling himself Grand Emperor. He died in the 5th year of Tiantong.

bio_md:
# 武成帝 · 主要事迹

高湛，高欢第九子。皇建二年孝昭崩，湛即位，改元太宁，次年改元河清。武成帝即位之初，尚有可称：太宁元年颁行律令，河清年间修撰《齐律》，为北齐法制之成就；又以斛律光等宿将为辅，与北周对峙，北齐疆域尚称稳固。

然武成帝「荒淫无度」：史载其「奢淫骄纵」，宠幸和士开等佞臣，朝政日坏；河清四年，禅位太子高纬，自称太上皇，「犹预国政」，而天统年间宠臣弄权更甚。武成之世，北齐由盛转衰：斛律光等名将渐被疏远，佞幸把持朝政，「齐政之衰，自武成始」。

天统五年，武成崩于晋阳，年三十二。史评武成：「荒淫委任佞幸，为齐衰张本。」北齐之亡，不亡于后主一朝，而亡于武成之荒纵：杀贤臣、任佞幸、禅位自娱，北齐之弊政，皆自武成开其端。

> 参考：点校本《北齐书》卷007《武成纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Zhan, ninth son of Gao Huan, took the throne after Xiaozhao's death in the 2nd year of Huangjian, changing the eras to Taining and then Heqing. His opening years had something to show: in the 1st year of Taining he issued the statutes, and in the Heqing years the *Qi Code* was compiled — the legal achievement of Northern Qi; with the veterans like Hulü Guang beside him, he held the line against Northern Zhou, and the borders of Qi held.

But he "sank into debauchery without limit": the records tell of his "extravagance and arrogance," his favoring of the flatterer He Shikai, and the government rotted; in the 4th year of Heqing he abdicated to his heir Gao Wei and styled himself Grand Emperor, "still taking part in the government," while in the Tiantong years the favorites' power grew worse. The turn of Qi from strength to decline came in his reign: the great generals like Hulü Guang were pushed aside, the favorites held the court — "the decline of Qi's government began with Wucheng."

He died at Jinyang in the 5th year of Tiantong at thirty-two. The histories say: "debauched, trusting flatterers, he laid the ground of Qi's decline." Qi did not fall in the Last Sovereign's reign alone; it fell to Wucheng's license — slaying the worthy, trusting the favorites, abdicating to his pleasures: the diseases of Qi all began with him.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Wucheng").
